text: Lesson 23 scoped Patient Scheduling Application Service as the Technical Service to build. Now it gets built out of real configuration items, each one using the correct subclass from Chapter One's cmdb_ci table hierarchy, and real relationships from Chapter Two connecting them — not a generic, undocumented pile of boxes.

Four CIs, four subclasses. Patient Scheduling App is a cmdb_ci_appl record — the software itself, not its hardware. SCHED-APP-01 and SCHED-APP-02 are cmdb_ci_win_server records, two load-balanced Windows servers running IIS. SCHED-SQL-01 is a cmdb_ci_db_instance, the SQL Server instance holding appointment records, provider calendars, and waitlists. SCHED-LB-01 is a cmdb_ci_lb_device, the load balancer distributing traffic across the two app servers.

A CI with no relationships barely tells you more than that it exists. Patient Scheduling App runs on both SCHED-APP-01 and SCHED-APP-02. Both servers depend on the single shared database instance, SCHED-SQL-01 — the relationship that matters most for impact analysis, since database maintenance ripples upward to both servers and the application without either server itself changing. SCHED-LB-01's load-balancing relationship to each server is documented explicitly, not assumed.

Building this in the right order matters: create the four CIs first, then wire the relationships between them in the correct direction, and finally add the one relationship that touches the EHR platform — nothing more than that single connection.

Lesson 23 drew a hard boundary around the EHR platform's own infrastructure. That connection is still real, so it gets exactly one relationship: Patient Scheduling App sends data to the existing EHR Integration Service, the Technical Service that already represents the EHR's side of that handoff elsewhere in the CMDB. No new CIs get created for it.

With four CIs and their relationships in place, the dependency chain now reads clearly, top to bottom, exactly as leadership asked for. Next: mapping this Technical Service up to the Business Service, deciding where Discovery takes over, and validating the result against the CMDB Health Dashboard.
